question.leadin: A palace in this city contains portraits of all of its rulers except one, whose portrait was replaced by a black sheet as punishment for treason.
question.text: Name this Italian city at the end of the Adriatic Sea which was a merchant republic ruled by doges such as Enrico Dandolo and dominated Mediterranean commerce for centuries.
question.answerHtml: the Most Serene Republic of Venice [or Venezia, or La Serenissimà]
question.answer: the Most Serene Republic of Venice
question.clue: This republic's leaders participated in the annual "Marriage of the Sea" ceremony using the ceremonial raft Bucentaur.

swap.leadin: This man's best-known military campaign saw victories at Palermo and Milazzo.
swap.text: Name this Italian general known as "the Father of Italian Independence" who led the Expedition of the Thousand in 1860.
swap.clue: The Battles of Calatafimi and Milazzo occurred before this man's biggest battle at Volturno.

question.leadin: Name these Italian cities important to Renaissance politics.
question.text: This Lombard city and former seat of the Visconti was once reconquered from France by Ludovico Sforza, known as "Il Moro;" it eventually passed to the Habsburgs.
question.clue: This city's last independent ruler was Ludovico il Moro, and Gian Galeazzo and Filippo Maria were members of this city's Visconti family.

swap.leadin: This man created the Rome-Berlin Axis with Adolf Hitler.
swap.text: Name this fascist dictator of Italy known as Il Duce, or "the Boss," who took power after a March on Rome.
swap.clue: He later ran Il Popolo D'Italia and nurtured a grudge against the Socialists for expelling him.

question.leadin: Senussi Rebels resisted this country's occupation of their homeland, Tripolitania.
question.text: Name this European power that unified in 1871 under Victor Emmanuel II. It conquered the province of Libya from the Ottoman Empire in 1911.
question.clue: In 1939, this country overthrew King Zog during its invasion of Albania.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Italian History.
swap.text: Name this King of Italy at the time of the Lateran Treaty who dismissed Mussolini after the great failures of the Italian military in World War II.
swap.clue: A member of the House of Savoy, this man saw the rise and fall of Mussolini during his reign as King of Italy.

question.text: This grandfather of Lorenzo de Medici was a skillful statesman during the Italian Renaissance, doing things like keeping councillors in the Florentine Signoria loyal to him. He was succeeded by his son, Piero.
question.clue: This man persuaded Pope Eugene IV to move the Council of Ferrara to his city, thereby attracting Byzantine wealth and learning.

swap.text: This conservative ally of Garibaldi, the prime minister of Piedmont, became the first prime minister of unified Italy under his monarch, Victor Emanuel II.
swap.answerHtml: Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour [accept either underlined name]
swap.clue: This politician negotiated the Treaty of Plombieres with Napoleon III, who agreed to support his cause.

question.leadin: The monarch of the losing side in this battle was taken to Spain and forced to sign the Treaty of Madrid in its aftermath.
question.text: Identify this 1525 victory for Charles V over Francis I in the Italian Wars.
question.clue: Alfonso d'Avalos, the Marquis of Pescara, led the arquebusiers under the overall command of Charles de Lannoy; he breached the wall of Mirabello around midnight and many combatants drowned in the nearby Ticino River.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about banking in Renaissance Italy.
swap.text: This city's Bank of St. George was opened in 1407 to manage public debt. Bank officials, in lieu of city administrators, directly governed this city's colonies of Corsica and Caffa.
swap.clue: A territory ruled by this city was attacked in 1553 by a joint Franco-Ottoman force under Turgut Reis.

question.text: This family produced Pope Alexander VI, who was the father its other notable members Cesare and Lucrezia.
question.clue: One member of this family authored the Treaty of Tordesillas and had his rival Savonarolla executed.

swap.leadin: This conflict was ended by the Peace of Caltabellotta, which confirmed Charles II as King of Naples, and Frederick III as the King of Trinacria.
swap.text: Name this conflict, which began with a wave of anti-French violence in Palermo, and an eventual uprising against Charles of Anjou.
swap.clue: That king attempted to end this conflict by challenging Peter III of Aragon to personal combat with Edward I serving as the judge of the contest.

question.text: Many of Boniface's policies were opposed by this medieval faction, which supported the Holy Roman Emperor over the Papacy.
question.clue: Before winning the battle of Montaperti, this group agreed to the Peace of Constance after it lost the Battle of Legnano, in which it was opposed by the Lombard League.

swap.leadin: Theodoric the Great personally killed Odoacer at a banquet in this city during their 18-day joint rule.
swap.text: Name this capital city of Italy under Odoacer and Theodoric. The Byzantine exarchs of Italy ruled from this city.
swap.clue: It became the seat of the Byzantine governor of Italy in the sixth century, and its namesake Cosmography was written around 700.

question.leadin: The Battle of Cannae took place in this modern-day region.
question.text: Name this southeastern region of Italy which became a duchy under Robert Guiscard in 1059. Frederick II constructed a getaway at Castel del Monte in this region, which became a favorite residence of Hohenstaufen rulers.

swap.text: This document, signed between Elizabeth I, Henry II, and Philip II resulted in the end of the Italian War of 1551 to 1559. Venice remained the only powerful independent constituent of the Italian Peninsula after its passage.
swap.clue: That side held a jousting tournament to celebrate this treaty, where Gabriel Montgomery had a sliver break of from his lance and pierce the king's eye, in the presence of surgeon Ambroise Par´e.

question.leadin: Name these places ruled by the Gonzaga family.
question.text: In 1536, Federico II Gonzaga gained control of this region in Piedmont from a branch of the Palaiologos [pay-lee-AH-loh-gos] family. A nobleman from this region founded the Kingdom of Thessalonica after leading the Fourth Crusade in the conquest of Constantinople.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the military career of Giuseppe Garibaldi.
swap.text: This volunteer unit, created in 1859 by Garibaldi in Cuneo, saw action in the second and third wars for Italian independence, including their invasion of Trentino in 1866 and victory at the Battle of Bezzecca.

question.leadin: According to Toponymity: An Atlas of Words, a dye was renamed for this battle "to make it seem like a more hip and of-the-moment color."
question.text: Identify this defeat for Austrian troops commanded by General Franz Gyulai during the Second Italian War of Independence. Maurice de MacMahon was later named duke of the site of this battle.
question.clue: The turning point of this battle was the arrival of reinforcements from Novara under the Marshal Francois de Certain-Canrobert, which beat back an assault at Ponte Vecchio.

swap.leadin: During this period, right-wing extremists founded the "New Order Scholarship Center", which was banned as a fascist group. FTPE.
swap.text: Name this period of political instability, marked by the violence of paramilitary organizations such as the October 22 Group. This period is often said to run from the death of Antionio Annarumma in 1969 through to the Salerno Massacre in 1982.
swap.clue: This period was preceded by a series of violent strikes known as the Hot Autumn.
